title: The Dark Night of the Soul
author: St John of the Cross
description: The Dark Night of the Soul by St John of the Cross (1542-1591), Spanish Carmelite friar, poet, reformer with St Teresa of Avila and Doctor of the Church. The treatise is a commentary on his poem 'En una noche oscura' ('On a dark night'), written around 1584-86 as a continuation of The Ascent of Mount Carmel. It describes the passive purgations by which God purifies the soul on the way to mystical union. Book One treats the night of the senses, analysing the spiritual versions of the seven deadly sins found in beginners and the aridity that weans the soul from consolations. Book Two treats the deeper night of the spirit, in which contemplative light experienced as darkness strips the intellect, memory and will before union in love. A cornerstone of Christian apophatic mysticism, it gave the world the phrase 'dark night of the soul' and remains central to spiritual direction and contemplative psychology.
